_about: Step-slice cases (slice.py): one work item, run from step-plan to the end of its inner loop on a fixture repository. The prompt is the step's request; work_item is what the seed records as the plan's only item; checks run in a clean export of the product worktree's HEAD; expect_paths are fnmatch patterns the item's commits must touch. A case with a seeded_defect plants a latent defect its own checks do not exercise: probe commands (run by seeded_defects.py on the final tree, never part of the verdicts) fail when the defect survived, and tree names the reference trees under fixtures/ (naive: what a run with no review leaves; fixed: the corrected tree) that prove the probe tells them apart. Experiment cases (experiment.py, experiments.json) may add seed_records ({stage: fields} merged into the synthetic result of each stage the seed records, so a seed at test-spec carries a step plan), seed_state ({env, from}: a local target outside the checkout that keeps state, pre-loaded from a fixture; slice.seed_state), focused (the item's focused command an evaluator reruns) and stand_ins (fixtures/stand-ins/<case>/<name>: alternative implementations an evaluator swaps into the final tree).

node-add-function.prompt: In this Node.js project, add a function slugify(text) to src/strings.js and export it. It lower-cases the text, turns every run of characters that are not a-z or 0-9 into one hyphen, and trims hyphens from both ends: slugify('  Hello, World! ') returns 'hello-world' and slugify('') returns ''. A non-string argument throws a TypeError, like the other helpers. Cover it with node:test tests; npm test must pass.

work_item.context: Lower-case; each run of non [a-z0-9] characters becomes one hyphen; trim hyphens at both ends; TypeError for a non-string; node:test tests.

Fix the bug and add a regression test; npm test must pass.

work_item.title: Fix paginate() dropping the last partial page
work_item.context: paginate([1,2,3,4,5], 3, 2) must return { page: 3, pages: 3, items: [5] }; add a regression test.

The argument is not changed, and a non-array argument throws a TypeError. Cover it with node:test tests; npm test must pass.

stand-in-parser.prompt: In this Node.js project, add a new module src/records.js exporting parseRecords(text) and select(records, field, value). parseRecords reads one record per non-blank line; a line holds fields `key=value` joined by `;`, a key is a lower-case letter followed by lower-case letters, digits or underscores, and values are trimmed: parseRecords('name=ada;team=x\n\nname=bob;team=y') returns [{name:'ada',team:'x'},{name:'bob',team:'y'}]. It rejects malformed input: a field with no `=`, an empty or invalid key, or a key repeated on one line throws a SyntaxError whose message names the 1-based line number; a non-string argument throws a TypeError. select returns the records whose field equals value, in input order (select(rows,'team','x') on the rows above returns the first record only); a non-array records throws a TypeError. Cover it with node:test tests; npm test must pass.

work_item.title: Add parseRecords and select in src/records.js
work_item.context: Exact oracles in the request; malformed input is rejected with SyntaxError naming the line.

criteria.text: parseRecords returns one object per non-blank line with trimmed values. Confirm by: the focused command; pass when TC-1 passes. Exercised. Serves R-1.
select returns the matching records in input order. Confirm by: the focused command; pass when TC-2 passes. Exercised. Serves R-1.
Malformed input throws SyntaxError naming the line; a non-string or non-array throws TypeError. Confirm by: the focused command; pass when TC-3 and TC-4 pass. Exercised. Serves R-1.

ui-component.prompt: In this project of plain-JS web components, add a <choice-confirm> component in src/choice-confirm.js and show it in index.html. It renders a list of options given by its `options` attribute (comma-separated; a name starting with `!` is shown but cannot be chosen), a Confirm button and a status line. Clicking an option selects it (only one at a time, marked with aria-pressed). Confirm with a choosable option selected shows `Confirmed: <name>` and dispatches a `confirm` event with the name; Confirm with no selection, or with an option that cannot be chosen, changes nothing and shows `Choose an available option first`. The interaction must be verified by tests that run it, not only by reading the code.

work_item.title: Add <choice-confirm> with select-then-confirm and refusal
work_item.context: Stateful select then confirm; an illegal choice or no selection is refused with a status line.

stand-in-rules.prompt: In this Node.js project, add a new module src/orders.js exporting parseOrders(text) and total(orders). parseOrders reads one order per non-blank line; a line holds fields `key=value` joined by `;` with keys id, qty, price, status and shipped_at, and values are trimmed. It returns objects {id, qty, price, status, shippedAt}: id, qty and price are numbers, status is lower-cased, shippedAt is the shipped_at text ('' when empty). parseOrders('id=1;qty=2;price=150;status=Open;shipped_at=\n\nid=2;qty=1;price=99;status=shipped;shipped_at=2026-10-01') returns [{id:1,qty:2,price:150,status:'open',shippedAt:''},{id:2,qty:1,price:99,status:'shipped',shippedAt:'2026-10-01'}]. Rules, each naming the 1-based line in its message: qty must be a whole number of at least 1 and price whole cents of at least 0, else RangeError; a field with no `=`, a status other than open or shipped, or a shipped_at that is not YYYY-MM-DD throws SyntaxError; and the fields must agree: a shipped order needs a shipped_at date and an open order must not have one, else SyntaxError. A non-string argument throws TypeError. total(orders) returns the sum of qty * price in cents (399 for the example) and must call meter.tick() from src/meter.js exactly once per order: its budget is one tick per order, far below the meter's hard limit of 10,000 ticks, past which the meter throws. Cover it with node:test tests; npm test must pass.

work_item.context: Exact oracles and rules in the request; each rule names the line; total's budget is one meter tick per order.

total returns the sum of qty * price and calls meter.tick() exactly once per order. Confirm by: the focused command; pass when TC-5 passes. Exercised. Serves R-1.
